From Daniel

Most homeowners I meet were only ever shown one way to sell — list it and hope, or take the first investor offer that lands in the mailbox. Both can leave real money behind. My job is to put all four options on the table with honest numbers, then let you decide. Even if you're just thinking about selling, the breakdown is free — and it's yours to keep whether we ever work together or not.

Fair questions

The things homeowners ask me before they ask for the breakdown.

What does the breakdown cost?

Nothing. It's free and there's no obligation. If one of the four options makes sense for you and you want my help executing it, we'll talk then.

“Renovate with no money out of pocket” — how does that work?

The upgrades are handled through a renovation partner program and the cost is paid out of the sale at closing — not from your bank account while you wait. In your breakdown I'll show you which upgrades actually move the price on a home like yours, and which ones don't pay for themselves.

Is a cash offer a lowball?

It's a trade, and I'll show you both sides of it honestly: cash is faster and more certain — no showings, no repairs, no buyer financing falling apart — and in exchange it's usually below what the open market would pay. For some situations (inherited homes, tight timelines, major repairs) it's the right trade. For others it isn't. The breakdown exists so you can see the size of the trade before you make it.

What does “flip your own house” actually mean?

Instead of selling cheap to an investor who renovates and resells your home for a profit, the renovation is done on your home, for your sale — you stay the owner and keep the profit the investor would have taken. It takes longer than a cash offer, and it's not right for every home. Your breakdown will show you if yours qualifies and what the numbers look like.

I'm not sure I'm selling at all. Is this still worth it?

Yes — that's exactly who I built it for. Knowing what each option nets you today is useful information whether you sell this year or in five years.
